# Jamstack Engineering Rules

## Decoupling & Architecture
- Decouple the frontend entirely from the backend.
- Communicate via versioned APIs.
- Prioritize Static Site Generation (SSG) for non-personalized content.
- Use Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) to update static content without full rebuilds.
- Use API-first design for all services.
- Prefer managed services for Auth, CMS, and Search.

## Performance & Delivery
- Deploy the frontend to a global Content Delivery Network (CDN).
- Ensure every deployment is atomic.
- Maintain instant rollback capability via CDN pointer switching.
- Prioritize HTML-first approaches.
- Minimize client-side JavaScript.
- Use lazy-loading for non-critical scripts.

## Serverless & Dynamic Logic
- Move dynamic server-side logic to serverless functions.
- Run personalization and geolocation logic at the edge.
- Keep the frontend stateless.
- Store persistent user state in client-side tokens or remote databases accessed via API.

## Edge Functions

- Distinguish edge functions (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Runtime, Deno Deploy) from serverless functions. Edge functions run in a restricted V8 isolate: no Node.js built-ins, limited CPU time, and no persistent file system.
- Use edge functions exclusively for latency-sensitive, stateless operations: auth token validation, request rewriting, A/B routing, and geolocation-based redirects.
- Do not perform database queries, secret fetching, or heavy computation inside an edge function. Offload these to a regional serverless function or origin service.
- Treat the edge runtime as a network boundary. Validate and sanitize any data passed from edge functions to origin services as you would external input.
- Test edge functions in a local edge runtime emulator (e.g., `wrangler dev`, `vercel dev`) before deployment. Do not rely solely on unit tests that run in Node.js; the runtime difference matters.

## Environment & Secrets

- Separate build-time variables (bundled into the artifact) from runtime variables (injected at request time by the CDN or edge layer). Build-time variables are baked into every cached copy; they cannot be changed without a rebuild.
- Never embed secrets, API keys, or credentials in build-time variables. Secrets accessible to client-side JavaScript are public; use runtime environment variables injected in server-side or edge code only.
- Prefix client-safe variables explicitly (e.g., `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, `GATSBY_`). Every variable without this prefix must be treated as server-only and never referenced in client-side bundles.
- Manage secrets in a dedicated secrets store (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or platform-equivalent). Do not store secrets in `.env` files committed to version control.
- Rotate API keys and tokens on a defined schedule and immediately on suspected exposure. Invalidate the old key before removing it from the secrets store to avoid a gap in availability.

## Core Web Vitals & Performance Budgets

- Measure LCP, CLS, and INP on every release using real-user monitoring (RUM) or synthetic testing (Lighthouse CI, WebPageTest). Do not rely solely on local profiling.
- Define a performance budget for LCP (≤2.5 s on a 4G connection) and CLS (≤0.1). Block deployments that regress either metric beyond the budget threshold in CI.
- Attribute CWV regressions to their source before shipping: third-party scripts, unoptimized images, and render-blocking resources are the most common causes.
- Track INP (Interaction to Next Paint) for content-heavy or interactive pages. An INP above 200 ms signals that main-thread work must be deferred or moved off-thread.

## Third-Party Scripts

- Load every non-critical third-party script with `defer` or `async`. Synchronous third-party scripts in `<head>` block the parser and are forbidden.
- Apply `integrity` (Subresource Integrity) hashes to all third-party scripts loaded from external CDNs. Omit integrity only for scripts served from a domain you control.
- Include third-party origins in `Content-Security-Policy` explicitly. A wildcard (`*`) in `script-src` nullifies CSP protection.
- Audit third-party scripts quarterly. Remove scripts whose owning service is no longer in use. Every retained script adds attack surface and performance cost.

## Engineering Standards
- Trigger automated builds and preview environments for every commit.
- Validate Core Web Vitals, accessibility (axe-core or equivalent), and broken links in preview environment checks before merging.
- Automate image compression, CSS minification, and font optimization in pipelines.
- Use `Content-Security-Policy` (CSP) headers.
- Enforce secure token handling at the system boundary.
